housing.title: Neighborhood housing survey
housing.question: Estimate the mean of block-group median house values in this fixed LA-area teaching frame. Compare geographically spread sampling with visiting selected tiles.
housing.population: 1990 California census block groups within latitude 33.6–34.6 and longitude −118.8–−117.6, deterministically thinned to at most 2,200 units. The target is this bundled frame, not all California households.
housing.layout: Actual latitude/longitude. Geographic tiles and four latitude-band strata are analytical groupings, not county boundaries. The observation is a block-group median, not an individual house price.
housing.recommended: Stratified proportional or two-stage geographic sampling
housing.source: Pace & Barry (1997), California Housing; archive used by scikit-learn
housing.license: Original research dataset; retain Pace & Barry attribution and source links.
housing.preprocessing: Filter the stated bounding rectangle, sort latitude/longitude/source row, retain every ceil(N/2200)-th row, divide housing value by 1000. Original values are capped at 500001 in the source.

steel.title: Steel-plant energy audit
steel.question: Estimate average interval energy use across the recorded 28-day plant audit. Compare stratifying operating loads with inspecting whole days or taking periodic meter readings.
steel.population: The first 28 recorded dates of the UCI steel-industry dataset from a South Korean plant. Each unit is one 15-minute meter record.
steel.layout: Calendar heatmap: rows are actual dates and columns are 15-minute clock slots. Load-type strata come from the source; clusters are dates. No production-line measurements are invented.
steel.recommended: Stratified proportional by load type; examine systematic aliasing
steel.source: Sathishkumar V E, Shin & Cho (2021), UCI Steel Industry Energy Consumption, DOI 10.24432/C52G8C
steel.preprocessing: Take the first 28 distinct recorded dates. Retain Usage_kWh without changing measurements.

bikes.title: Bike-share demand study
bikes.question: Estimate mean hourly rentals for this fixed winter-period frame. Compare covering each time-of-day band with surveying only convenient early records or a few whole days.
bikes.population: Hourly Capital Bikeshare rental counts for the first 90 recorded dates in the UCI 2011–2012 dataset. These are system totals, not station-level counts.
bikes.layout: Date × hour demand heatmap. Five time-of-day strata and day clusters are derived from real timestamps. Blank cells were not recorded and are not sampling units.
bikes.recommended: Stratified sampling across time of day
bikes.preprocessing: Take first 90 dates and retain cnt as recorded; derive five time-of-day bands.

air.title: Roadside air-quality monitoring
air.question: Estimate the mean of the available hourly NO₂ readings. Compare spreading measurements across time bands with visiting only selected days.
air.population: Available NO₂ reference-analyzer readings during the first 28 calendar dates of the UCI Italian-city Air Quality record. Missing -200 values are excluded, not set to zero.
air.layout: Date × hour heatmap from one roadside monitoring site, not a network of invented neighborhoods. Four time-of-day strata; days are unequal-size clusters after missing readings are removed.
air.recommended: Stratified time-of-day monitoring; unequal-size day clusters
air.source: De Vito et al. (2008), UCI Air Quality, DOI 10.24432/C59K5F
air.license: UCI lists CC BY 4.0 and retains an author research-only note. This bundled frame is for academic teaching/research.
air.preprocessing: Retain the first 28 calendar dates; remove missing NO2(GT)=-200 and NA. Do not impute excluded hours.

oats.title: Oat field-trial yield survey
oats.units: Yates yield units (¼ lb per subplot)
oats.question: Estimate mean yield across the 72 recorded subplots. Compare covering all nitrogen treatment groups with selecting entire field blocks.
oats.population: All 72 subplots in the nlme Oats split-plot trial: six blocks, three oat varieties, and four nitrogen concentrations. The target is the finite recorded trial, not a causal treatment-effect estimate.
oats.layout: Schematic block × variety/nitrogen subplot grid. Blocks and treatments are real; displayed within-block order groups treatments for teaching and is not claimed to be the original field position.
oats.recommended: Stratify by assigned treatment; compare whole-block sampling
oats.source: Yates (1935), via Pinheiro & Bates nlme Oats dataset; Rdatasets mirror
oats.license: Source nlme package: GPL (>=2); retain dataset and publication attribution.
oats.preprocessing: Retain all 72 yields. Derive nitrogen strata and field-block clusters. Reorder the display by block, variety and nitrogen.

shafts.title: Machined shafts on a conveyor (generated)
shafts.question: Estimate mean diameter across the production run. Compare a random-start systematic inspection with random sampling, then turn on a periodic machining problem.
shafts.population: 1,200 generated shafts in production order. A tool is replaced every 200 shafts; a small wear trend restarts after replacement. Each unit is one shaft.
shafts.layout: A wrapped production-order heatmap: 50 consecutive shafts per displayed row, not 24 separate physical lines. Tool runs are real groups within this generated model; cartons contain 50 shafts.
shafts.recommended: Systematic random-start inspection for routine coverage; compare with SRS when periodic faults are present
shafts.mechanism: Diameter = 20 mm + centered linear wear within each 200-shaft tool run + small run offset + independent normal measurement/process noise. Optional period-20 oscillation illustrates systematic aliasing.
shafts.source: Generated engineering teaching data; context reference only, not measured field data.
shafts.license: Values are generated by this app; no third-party measurements are reproduced.
shafts.preprocessing: Diameter = 20 mm + centered linear wear within each 200-shaft tool run + small run offset + independent normal measurement/process noise. Optional period-20 oscillation illustrates systematic aliasing. All numeric benchmarks and tolerances are illustrative, not acceptance specifications.

production_lines.title: Parts from five production lines (generated)
production_lines.question: Estimate the plant-wide mean across unequal production volumes. Compare proportional and equal allocation, and explain why equal allocation needs population weights.
production_lines.population: 1,380 generated parts: line volumes 480, 360, 240, 180 and 120. Each unit is one part; line means and process SDs differ.
production_lines.layout: Five horizontal production lines. Colored cells are individual parts in within-line production order. Empty cells beyond shorter line lengths are not units. Lots contain up to 30 parts.
production_lines.recommended: Stratified random sampling by production line, with proportional allocation and known line-volume weights
production_lines.mechanism: Five normal line processes have mean offsets 0, +0.025, −0.020, +0.040 and −0.035 mm, SDs 0.010, 0.020, 0.015, 0.030 and 0.012 mm, and a small within-line drift.
production_lines.source: Generated engineering teaching data; context reference only, not measured field data.
production_lines.license: Values are generated by this app; no third-party measurements are reproduced.
production_lines.preprocessing: Five normal line processes have mean offsets 0, +0.025, −0.020, +0.040 and −0.035 mm, SDs 0.010, 0.020, 0.015, 0.030 and 0.012 mm, and a small within-line drift. All numeric benchmarks and tolerances are illustrative, not acceptance specifications.

pallets.title: Component inspection in warehouse pallets (generated)
pallets.question: Estimate mean component resistance. Compare inspecting more pallets with inspecting more components per pallet at a similar total measurement cost.
pallets.population: 36 generated pallets from three suppliers. Pallet sizes cycle through 24, 30, 36 and 42 components; there are 1,188 components in total. Each unit is one component.
pallets.layout: Warehouse rack view with a 6×6 arrangement of pallets. Pallet detail shows components in schematic carton positions. Shared pallet offsets create similarity within a pallet.
pallets.recommended: Two-stage sampling: randomly select pallets, then randomly select components inside each pallet
pallets.mechanism: Resistance = 100 ohm + supplier offset (−2, 0, +2) + a shared normal pallet offset (SD 2.5 ohm) + independent component noise (SD 1.2 ohm). Unequal pallet sizes require the design weights.
pallets.source: Generated engineering teaching data; context reference only, not measured field data.
pallets.license: Values are generated by this app; no third-party measurements are reproduced.
pallets.preprocessing: Resistance = 100 ohm + supplier offset (−2, 0, +2) + a shared normal pallet offset (SD 2.5 ohm) + independent component noise (SD 1.2 ohm). Unequal pallet sizes require the design weights. All numeric benchmarks and tolerances are illustrative, not acceptance specifications.

asphalt.title: Asphalt pavement thickness (generated)
asphalt.question: Estimate mean pavement thickness while spreading cores across the paving work. Compare mean estimation with the chance of detecting a localized thin patch.
asphalt.population: 720 generated potential core locations on a 1,200 m × 7.2 m two-lane pavement. Six 200 m sublots are strata; twelve 100 m segments are clusters.
asphalt.layout: Plan-view road heatmap using distance and transverse offset. Lane markings and sublot boundaries show placement groups. Values are hypothetical thickness at candidate locations, not real cores.
asphalt.recommended: Stratified random core locations within every paving sublot
asphalt.mechanism: Thickness = 80 mm + a smooth longitudinal wave + lane offsets ±1.5 mm + independent noise (SD 2 mm). An optional localized Gaussian-shaped thin patch is centered near station 850 m and offset 5.4 m.
asphalt.source: Generated engineering teaching data; context reference only, not measured field data.
asphalt.license: Values are generated by this app; no third-party measurements are reproduced.
asphalt.preprocessing: Thickness = 80 mm + a smooth longitudinal wave + lane offsets ±1.5 mm + independent noise (SD 2 mm). An optional localized Gaussian-shaped thin patch is centered near station 850 m and offset 5.4 m. All numeric benchmarks and tolerances are illustrative, not acceptance specifications.

concrete.title: Concrete delivery loads and slab placement (generated)
concrete.question: Estimate average strength across delivery loads. Distinguish sampling more truckloads from making more specimens from the same truckload.
concrete.population: 80 generated equal-volume concrete deliveries, each linked to one schematic slab zone. Every delivery has three correlated 28-day specimen results; the load average is the sampling outcome, so N=80 loads, not 240 specimens.
concrete.layout: Concrete truck sequence linked to an 8×10 slab-placement map. Adjacent delivery groups share a batching effect. Three cylinders are nested within each delivery; slab positions are schematic.
concrete.recommended: Simple random sampling of delivery loads; specimens from one load remain nested observations
concrete.mechanism: Load strength = 36 MPa + supplier offset (0, −2, +2) + shared four-load batch noise (SD 1.2 MPa) + load noise (SD 1.6 MPa) + a small delivery-order effect. Each of three specimens adds SD 0.75 MPa noise. Slump is generated separately and is not used as a strength predictor.
concrete.source: Generated engineering teaching data; context reference only, not measured field data.
concrete.license: Values are generated by this app; no third-party measurements are reproduced.
concrete.preprocessing: Load strength = 36 MPa + supplier offset (0, −2, +2) + shared four-load batch noise (SD 1.2 MPa) + load noise (SD 1.6 MPa) + a small delivery-order effect. Each of three specimens adds SD 0.75 MPa noise. Slump is generated separately and is not used as a strength predictor. All numeric benchmarks and tolerances are illustrative, not acceptance specifications.
